reader.summary: This week in India was dominated by the youth-led 'Cockroach' (CJP) protests over voter-roll purges, which escalated as leaders were arrested and released in rapid succession, demonstrators marched on the Election Commission demanding the CEC's resignation, and UN experts urged the government to stop using excessive force. Farmers joined the movement, and Prime Minister Modi found himself on the defensive. Simultaneously, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio visited India, toured the world's largest oil refinery at Jamnagar, and held talks in Mumbai aimed at finalizing a US-India trade deal that President Trump called 'pretty close.' On the economic front, Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms completed India's largest-ever IPO, fully subscribed within hours on $77 billion in bids, sending the rupee to a six-week high. A deadly stampede at a Durga Puja festival in Kolkata killed between 17 and 33 people, with sources disagreeing on the toll, dampening the holiday season. Indian shares slid on surging oil prices, and the RBI mounted a costly defense of the weakening rupee. Corporate earnings were mixed: Kotak Bank profit rose 29 percent and Adani Power doubled, while Swiggy fell to a record low. A cyberattack exposed customer records at the State Bank of India, and India's defense industry gained momentum from Europe's war.

key_events.event: CJP 'Cockroach' protest leaders were arrested, released, and re-arrested in rapid succession while demonstrators marched on the Election Commission and UN experts called on India to stop using excessive force.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio visited Jamnagar's world-largest oil refinery and held talks in Mumbai with Foreign Minister Jaishankar to finalize a US-India trade deal described as 'pretty close' by Trump.
Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms completed India's largest-ever IPO, becoming fully subscribed within hours on over $77 billion in anchor and retail bids.
A stampede at a Durga Puja festival in Kolkata killed between 17 and 33 people, with AP, BBC, and Bloomberg reporting different death tolls.
Surging oil prices dragged Indian shares to weekly losses while the RBI mounted a costly defense of the rupee, and small-cap stocks fell on margin liquidations.
A cyberattack on the State Bank of India exposed records of nearly 3,900 customers, the bank's largest data breach on record.
Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff was allegedly shot at by gunmen, reviving scrutiny of the film industry's gangster past.
India's trade minister said the India-EU trade deal could become operational in early 2027.
Corporate earnings were sharply mixed: Kotak Bank profit rose 29 percent and Adani Power doubled, while Swiggy hit a record low and Godrej Properties reported a profit slump.
India's defense industry gained momentum as Europe's war drove demand, and China border tensions remained in focus despite ongoing talks.

display.headline: India Protesters Force Voter Roll Review as Trade Deal Nears
emoji_reasons: The CJP voter-roll protests are the dominant and escalating story of the week.
The US-India trade deal is the second major thread, moving from talks to a published agreement.
The SBI cyberattack and the resulting banking-sector cybersecurity push make the digital/tech icon relevant.
display.tldr: Farmers and youth will march in multiple Indian cities demanding a voter-roll review, while New Delhi and Washington publish their trade agreement. A central bank inquiry will follow the SBI data breach. The CEC may resign under pressure.
display.eli5:
In India, a group of young people called the CJP are protesting because the government removed a huge number of names from the voter list. This week, farmers joined them, and the UN told the government to stop using too much force. Next week, even more people will march in different cities at the same time, and the government will have to promise to look into what happened to those voter names.

At the same time, the US and India are almost done negotiating a trade deal about tariffs and oil. The American secretary of state just visited a giant refinery in India, and both sides are expected to put the deal in writing next week.

Also, a hacker got into India's biggest bank and stole customer information. The central bank will start an investigation and make all banks follow new security rules.

A surprise would be the head of India's election body actually quitting their job because of all the pressure from the streets and the UN.

Founder Abhijeet Dipke and senior leaders were detained, released, and then jailed for five days after scaling barricades at a New Delhi rally. Police closed off iconic protest sites, and women staged separate demonstrations against police brutality. Journalists accused authorities of suppressing press freedom. Separately, at least 17 people died in a crush at a Hindu festival in Kolkata. - CJP protest crackdown (dominant, escalating): CJP founder Dipke and senior leaders were detained, released, and then jailed for five days after a New Delhi rally, India closed off an iconic protest park, women protested police brutality, and the Supreme Court agreed to hear related cases.
